decisive_items: At 12 months: En face OCT revealed hyperreflective tissues starting to proliferate on retinal vessels; OCTA B-scan showed pyramid-shaped proliferations
The patient's response to anti-VEGF injections and the progression of neovascularization on OCTA and fluorescein angiography support this diagnosis
response.rationale: The combination of macular edema, response to anti-VEGF injections, and subsequent development of hyperreflective tissues and angiogenic sprouts on retinal vessels, as well as the progression of neovascularization on OCTA and fluorescein angiography, is most consistent with Neovascular Age-related Macular Degeneration

rejected.why: Limited support from OCTA findings and lack of characteristic features of retinal angiomas
Hyperreflective tissues and angiogenic sprouts are not specific to retinal neovascularization
Initial resolution of macular edema with anti-VEGF injections does not rule out other diagnoses
Dendritic vascular-like structures can be seen in other conditions, and the patient's presentation is more consistent with neovascular age-related macular degeneration
